explanation: Despite its Polish-sounding name, it began in Bohemia and swept the ballrooms of Prague, Vienna and Paris within about a decade. One theory links the name to the Czech word půlka, 'half'.

claims.text: The polka originated in Bohemia, in present-day Czechia, in the 1830s.
The polka did not originate in Poland, Austria or Hungary.
Within about a decade the polka had become popular in the ballrooms of Prague, Vienna and Paris.
One theory derives the name 'polka' from the Czech word půlka, meaning half.
The polka is danced in duple time, with two beats to the bar.
